references.text: Joseph's interpretation of Pharaoh's dreams about seven years of abundance followed by seven years of severe famine, providing direct context for verse 31 that the abundance will not be remembered because of the ensuing famine.
The fulfillment of the prophecy: the famine began after the seven good years and affected all lands, confirming the severity described in verse 31 that the abundance would not be remembered.
Describes how the famine was extremely severe, so that the land of Egypt and Canaan wasted away from hunger, illustrating the seriousness of the famine prophesied in 41:31.
Refers to how God called a famine upon the land and broke all support of bread, a reference to God's sovereign rule that led to the famine in Egypt.
The psalm's promise of provision during famine highlights how God's people can withstand the harsh judgment warned of in Genesis.
Direct narrative fulfillment: 43:1 confirms that the severe famine foretold in 41:31 has occurred.
